title: Staged payload evolution and client feature negotiation playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook specifies an operational pattern for evolving request/response payloads and shipping server-side changes while preserving safe client compatibility. It pairs staged payload extensions with an explicit client negotiation header and client-side feature flags. The goal is to make schema evolution predictable, measurable, and reversible for both hosted and private deployments.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
- Backwards-compatible and additive schema changes (new optional fields, extended enums).
- Introduction of experimental fields that should be opt-in per client.
- Rolling out server-side behavior changes that require explicit client opt-in.
- Coordinating cross-service payload migrations where clients are deployed at varying cadences.

Key concepts and guarantees
---------------------------
- Compatibility tiers (server promises):
  - stable: field is safe for all clients; server must handle absence and presence consistently.
  - opt_in: server will treat the field as no-op unless client explicitly declares support.
  - experimental: short-lived, may be removed; enabled only via canary client population.

- Client capability negotiation: clients announce supported features via a single header X-Client-Capabilities containing a compact JSON map (base64 or URL-safe encoding allowed). Example header: X-Client-Capabilities: eyJ2IjoiMSIsImZlYXR1cmVzIjp7ImJhdGNoX3mdIjoiMSJ9fQ== (decoded -> {"v":"1","features":{"batch_v2":"1","safe_tags":"opt_in"}})

- Server adaptation layer: servers must contain a small, tested adaptors registry that maps capability sets -> effective response shape. Adaptors are feature-gated and exercised by contract tests.

Compatibility matrix (behavioral guarantees)
-------------------------------------------
| Change type             | Guarantee to older clients                   | Recommended strategy             |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Add optional field      | Ignore/strip for older clients                | Add as "stable" with default    |
| Add enum variant        | Map unknown enum to legacy fallback value     | Introduce with opt_in then stable|
| Change semantics        | Not allowed without opt_in and canary         | Use experimental then opt_in      |
| Remove field            | Deprecate for 6 months, then remove with warning | Deprecate -> remove              |

Client negotiation protocol
---------------------------
- Header name: X-Client-Capabilities
- Payload: JSON object with keys: version, features, client_id (optional), timestamp
- Encoding: RFC-safe base64 or URL-encoded JSON; servers must accept either.
- Server behavior: build an "effective policy" by merging default server flags with client-declared features.

Client capability JSON example (before encoding):
{
  "version": "1",
  "client_id": "web-frontend-12",
  "features": {
    "batch_v2": "opt_in",
    "precise_tokens": "stable"
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-03-10T14:22:00Z"
}

Migration rollout procedure (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------
1. Design: publish a short design note listing new fields, semantics, opt_in vs stable decision, and tests. Owner: product/engineering.
2. Contract tests: author a contract test suite that validates both old and new capability permutations. Add tests to CI.
3. Server implementation: add adaptor logic behind feature flags and a runtime toggle. Deploy to staging.
4. Canary: enable experimental fields for 1% of traffic from clients that advertise experimental capability. Monitor metrics for 72 hours.
5. Incremental opt-in: invite client teams to opt-in by setting X-Client-Capabilities or via client-side feature flag rollout.
6. Observability gate: require 0.1% error impact, <3% latency increase, no regression in quality metrics for canary to proceed.
7. Scale: increase traffic % in geometric steps (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%).
8. Stabilize: after 14 days at >=50% with no regressions, promote the field from opt_in to stable.
9. Deprecation (when removing): publish 6-month deprecation schedule and include server-side warning header X-Deprecated-Fields.

Rollout checklist (short)
-------------------------
- [ ] Design doc published and linked.
- [ ] Contract test coverage added (positive and negative cases).
- [ ] Staging deployment with flags.
- [ ] Canary launch and metrics monitored.
- [ ] Client opt-in instructions published.
- [ ] Post-mortem template ready for any regression.

Monitoring and SLOs
-------------------
- Essential metrics to collect per rollout:
  - feature_error_rate: errors on requests with feature enabled (SLO: <= 0.1% above baseline)
  - feature_latency_p50/p95: latency with feature (SLO: < 10% above baseline p95)
  - feature_quality_delta: if applicable, quality regression metric (custom per eval)
  - adoption_rate: number of distinct clients that advertise a capability

- Traces: add a tag feature.vector to spans to make it filterable in flame/trace views.
- Dashboards: create a short-lived rollout dashboard for each migration showing the above metrics vs baseline. Keep dashboards linked in the design doc.

Contract testing and CI requirements
----------------------------------
- Contract tests must run on:
  - server default (no capabilities)
  - explicit opt_in capability set
  - experimental capability set (if applicable)
  - mixed-client scenarios (requests from both old and new clients)
- Add a synthetic traffic job that periodically exercises edge cases (unknown enum values, missing optional fields).

Emergency rollback and mitigation
--------------------------------
1. Immediate toggle: flip runtime flag to ignore the experimental/opt_in fields and return legacy shape.
2. Rate-limit: if feature is resource-heavy, apply per-client rate limits and sticky routing away from overloaded shards.
3. Communication: page involved on-call list, update the rollout dashboard with red status, and create an incident ticket with the migration id.
4. Post-incident actions: root cause analysis, publish postmortem, revise playbook if needed.

Operational ownership and responsibilities
-----------------------------------------
- Feature owner: product or feature engineering team — responsible for design doc, adoption plan, and client communications.
- Runtime owner: serving/runtime team — responsible for adaptor code, flags, observability hooks, and rollback toggles.
- Quality owner: Applied ML / Evals (when change affects model outputs) — provides quality evaluation and acceptance criteria.

Examples and snippets
---------------------
- Sample server-side adaptor pseudocode:

// adaptor registration snippet (pseudo)
registerAdaptor("batch_v2", (req, capabilities) => {
  if (!capabilities.features.batch_v2) {
    return transformToLegacy(req);
  }
  return req; // support batch_v2 shape
});

- Sample curl using base64-encoded capability header:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Capabilities: eyJ2IjoiMSIsImZlYXR1cmVzIjp7ImJhdGNoX3YyIjoib3B0X2luIn19" -d '@payload.json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

JSON schema example (recommended minimal annotation):
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "prompt": {"type": "string"},
    "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "x-compatibility": "stable"},
    "priority": {"type": "string", "enum": ["low","medium","high"], "x-compatibility": "opt_in"}
  },
  "required": ["prompt"]
}

Related pages and references
----------------------------
- Link to schema-fencing playbook (referenced for deprecations and fence periods).
- Runtime feature-flagging standards page.

Appendix: Quick decision rubric for opt_in vs stable
---------------------------------------------------
- Opt_in when any of the following are true:
  - Behavioral semantics change (not just additional data).
  - Server will incur >5% CPU or memory increase for enabled requests.
  - Changes affect billing/chargeable token accounting.
- Promote to stable when:
  - 90% of active client surface supports the capability for 14 days, and
  - No increase in error rate beyond 0.1% and latency within SLOs.
